QUOTE: "It then calls `client.createPost` again. On success it writes the server post and updates the last-post time for the channel... On failure, the same error handling applies: the three "removal" errors delete the post, and everything else sets `failed: true` again."
VERDICT: HIT
WHY: The answer says retryFailedPost makes one new createPost call, and on failure it marks the post failed again or deletes it for the three errors. The "no loop or backoff" part is covered by "The app code does not retry" and "the user, not the app, decides when to retry".
